title: Correlated Hallucinations: Do Different Models Confidently Agree on the Same Wrong Facts?

original_idea.body:
# Correlated Hallucinations: Do Different Models Confidently Agree on the Same Wrong Facts?

**Problem:** Verification pipelines treat agreement across models as evidence of truth; if models share a blind spot, they hallucinate the same wrong fact in unison.

**Direction:** Curate ~150 fact questions including known popular-but-wrong answers. Query 6+ open models. Measure correlated wrong answers and whether agreement on wrong answers exceeds agreement on right answers.

**Why it matters:** Many cheap safety heuristics (self-consistency, majority-vote fact-checking) assume independence; correlated hallucination breaks them.

**Relevant context:** Artificial Hivemind; correlated-errors framework (arXiv 2506.07962).

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: correlated hallucination breaks consensus/majority-vote fact-checking, a concrete failure of cheap safety heuristics.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Curate ~150 fact questions, query open models, measure correlated wrong answers; accessible to beginners.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Tightly scoped: correlated-hallucination and false-confidence rate, clear deliverable.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Cheap consensus-fact-checking audit labs deprioritize; public models, no internal access.

low_compute.reasoning: Inference over a small QA set, one GPU or API/CPU-light.

novelty.reasoning: Correlated errors are studied; the specific correlated-hallucination-on-misconceptions angle may be open.
